messages:
eva: Bringing up peregrine-v0 (q5) on staging — quick smoke shows weird locale-specific regressions: Korean polite suffixes collapsing to informal forms, Chinese numerals being emitted as arabic digits in contexts where spelled numerals are expected, and Arabic RTL punctuation spacing/reflow issues. Anyone seen this pattern? @li-wei @sanjay :eyes:

li-wei: I ran a quick compare earlier on a different model. Can you paste a minimal repro and the eval harness commands you used?

eva: Repro (minimal):
```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_KEY\" \
  -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"peregrine-v0-q5","input":"선생님께서 말씀드리셨습니다: 감사드립니다.","max_tokens":64,"temperature":0}\n'\n```
Observed output (staging peregrine-v0-q5):
- Input (ko): "선생님께서 말씀드리셨습니다: 감사드립니다." \n- Output: "선생님 말했어: 고마워."  <-- lost honorific suffix, became informal

Example CN numeral case:
- Input: "订单号一二三四，请确认。"
- Output: "订单号1234，请确认。"  <-- numeric digits instead of spelled numerals (affects downstream NER/formatting)

Arabic RTL punctuation example:
- Input: "مرحبا، هل يمكنك المساعدة؟"
- Output: "مرحبا ,هل يمكنك المساعدة؟"  <-- space before comma, comma on LTR side

qa-bot: Auto-eval summary (today):
- ko-politeness-set: BLEU delta: -3.4
- cn-numeral-set: CER delta: +2.1
- ar-rtl-punct: Precision/Recall F1 delta: -15%

sanjay: Hypothesis: tokenizer/vocab mismatch or quantization merged embeddings for low-frequency suffix tokens leading to lower logits. Two quick checks: 1) diff tokenization vs baseline 2) compare logits for suffix tokens before/after quant.

mina: Note: The model checkpoint was bundled with tokenizer v2.1 artifacts, but our staging inference image defaults to tokenizer v2.0 unless pinned. That would explain subwordization shifts (different merges -> different token sequences). The Arabic punctuation spacing might be decoding side (detokenizer differences) though.

li-wei: Can you run this tokenization diff script? (quick snippet)
```
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
new = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer_v2.1.json')
old = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer_v2.0.json')
text = '선생님께서 말씀드리셨습니다: 감사드립니다.'
print('v2.1 ->', new.encode(text).tokens)
print('v2.0 ->', old.encode(text).tokens)
```
If token lists differ around honorific suffixes we pin the tokenizer in the model manifest.

sanjay: Also add `?trace=true` to the inference call and dump logits around the suffix tokens so we can see if probability mass shifted. If tokens exist in both tokenizers, compare argmax/logit gap.

eva: Plan of action I'm running now:
1) re-run tokenization with v2.0 and v2.1 to confirm diff
2) re-run generation with model pinned to tokenizer v2.0 image (quick smoke)
3) if tokenizer mismatch -> update onboarding checklist + pinner; if not -> bisect quant pipeline (q5 config) and collect logits

mina: FYI onboarding note: always include tokenizer.json SHA and vocab.tsv in the model bundle and assert on startup. I'll open a PR to add the assertion.

sanjay: If tokenizer pin fixes Korean and CN numeral cases but Arabic persists, check detokenizer/normalizer version mismatches (we had a recent CL that changed arabic punctuation spacing heuristics).

eva: Quick update 20m later: reran with tokenizer v2.0 (pinned) — Korean polite forms preserved in smoke set, CN numerals now match baseline (spelled numerals preserved). Arabic punctuation still flaky; suspect detok/normalize step. Conclusion: root cause = tokenizer mismatch + leftover detok regression. I'll follow up with a small bisect on the detok package and post logs here.

mina: Great — please paste the failing Arabic sample with `?trace=true` when you have it and I'll instrument the detok unit tests.

eva: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
